sentences.text:
This appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 by the Oriental Insurance Company, assailing the judgment and award dated 21.12.2009, in Claim Petition No.317 of 2003,
passed by the Claim Tribunal at Ahmedabad City.

2. According to case of the respondent-claimant, he met with an accident on 28.12.2000 when the Ambassador taxi wherein he was traveling, dashed against the utility jeep, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries resulting into permanent partial disablement.

The Claim Petition No.317 Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Rameshbhai Sankalchand Patel on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25435835/
1 of 2003 was filed against both the vehicles and their insurance companies.

entities.text: Claim Petition No.317 Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Rameshbhai Sankalchand Patel
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned tribunal vide its judgment and award dated 21.12.2009, awarded a sum of Rs.4,12,500/- with NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1797/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/10/2023 undefined interest @ 7.5%.
In the judgment, the tribunal apportioned the negligence in the proportionate of 70:30.
In other words, the car driver was held liable to the extent of 70%, whereas, the driver of the jeep held negligent to the extent of 30%.

3. The appellant-insurance company with whom the utility jeep was insured, has preferred the present appeal on a very limited ground that, driver of the jeep was not holding a valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and therefore, the liability to pay the compensation so far appellant-insurance company is concerned, cannot be saddled upon the company.
4. This Court has heard learned counsel Mr. Rathin Raval, Mr. Maulik Shelat and Mr. A.V. Prajapati for the respective parties.
5. Mr. Rathin Raval, learned counsel appearing for the appellant has submitted that, the tribunal erred in law, while holding the insurance company liable to pay the amount of compensation.

He submitted that, the driver of the vehicle was holding LMV (Non-transport License) whereas the utility jeep was a commercial vehicle and therefore, without any endorsement on the license by the competent authority permitting the driver to drive commercial vehicle, it cannot be said that, the driver was holding a valid license to drive the vehicle and thus, the said admitted facts having been ignored by the tribunal while holding the issue of liability on the part of the present appellant-insurance company.
 NEUTRAL CI  C/FA/1797/2010 ORDER DATED: 12/10/2023  undefined 6.

On the other hand, Mr. A.V. Prajapati, learned counsel supported the impugned judgment and award as well as findings thereof, fixing the liability of the present appellant and contended that, the claimant was third party and in case of third party, the insurance company cannot escape from its Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Rameshbhai Sankalchand Patel on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25435835/
2 liability to pay the amount of compensation.
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and on perusal of material placed on record, the issue falls for my consideration is to whether the appellant-insurance company disown its liability on the ground that, driver although duly licensed to drive LMV, but, there was no endorsement on the license to drive commercial vehicle?
8.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Rameshbhai Sankalchand Patel
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The issue as raised is not res integra.
The respondent- claimant is the third party so far utility jeep is concerned.

It is beneficial to refer the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Swaran Singh and others, (AIR 2004 SC 1531), wherein the Apex Court categorically held that mere absence, fake or invalid DL for driving at relevant time are not themselves defence available to the Insurance Companies against the third parties.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Swaran Singh and others, (AIR 2004 SC 1531)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further observed that to avoid the liability towards the insured, the Insurance Company has to prove that the owner, insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicle by duly license.

In the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., (2017 ACJ 2011), the Apex Court held that the LMV as defined would include a class of transport NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1797/2010 ORDER DATED:
12/10/2023 undefined vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2 (21) of the Act and,
therefore, no separate endorsement on the license is required to drive a transport vehicle.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., (2017 ACJ 2011)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In light of the settled position of law, and considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, the insurer appellant failed to establish the fact that the 'breach' was committed by the insured.
Unless and until the breach is not established, the insurance company cannot escape from its liability to pay the amount of compensation.
10. For the reasons recorded, the present appeal is failed and dismissed accordingly.
R & P be immediately sent to the Tribunal.
The Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount with accruing interest if any, to the claimant herein.
Decree be drawn accordingly.
